Lighthouses are typically painted with high-contrast color schemes, such as black and white horizontal stripes, to make them easily distinguishable from other coastal structures during the day.
Many modern lighthouses have been automated and converted into museums or tourist attractions, preserving their historical significance while reducing the need for resident keepers.
The light source in traditional lighthouses often used Fresnel lenses, which were invented in the early 19th century and are capable of projecting a beam of light over great distances with remarkable efficiency.
